title: Here’s Why Janus Henderson is Bullish On Meta Platforms, Inc. (META)
detail:
Here’s Why Janus Henderson is Bullish On Meta Platforms, Inc. (META)
Attiya Zainib
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:56 PM MST 3 min read
META
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Janus Henderson, an investment management company, released its "Global Sustainable Equity Fund " Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here. The Equity Fund returned 1.86% in the third quarter of 2026, matching its benchmark, while outperforming the IA Global peer group's 0.38% return. The fund's performance reflected a sharp rotation within the artificial intelligence trade: companies perceived as vulnerable to AI disruption recovered, while businesses tied to AI infrastructure, power, cooling, and electrification came under pressure. The portfolio's exposure to infrastructure-related companies and its lack of energy holdings weighed on relative performance, partly offset by gains from selected technology, healthcare, and financial investments. The managers continued to adjust the portfolio around their view that AI adoption will create opportunities for companies with durable competitive advantages, proprietary data, network effects, and resilient business models. The managers also highlighted growing electricity demand from data centres, the potential for renewable energy and battery investments to support energy security and decarbonisation, and the risks that a strong El Niño could pose to agriculture and inflation. Looking ahead, the fund remains focused on balancing AI-related growth opportunities with sustainability considerations, while favouring companies with pricing power, resilient operations, and long-term structural growth potential amid geopolitical uncertainty, elevated energy prices, and higher interest rates. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

In its third-quarter 2026 investor letter, Janus Henderson Global Sustainable Equity Fund discussed Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META). Meta Platforms, Inc. is a technology company that operates social media platforms and develops artificial intelligence products, digital advertising solutions, and virtual and augmented reality technologies. The one-month return of Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) was 17.69%, while its shares traded between $520.26 and $779.82 over the last 52 weeks. On October 30, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) stock closed at approximately $614.99 per share, with a market capitalization of about $1.56 trillion.

Janus Henderson Global Sustainable Equity Fund stated the following regarding Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"In September, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) launched Muse, a consumer AI agent that can shop around for anything from insurance to clothing on its users' behalf. Muse drew more than 500,000 users in its first week, including more than 250,000 daily active users. Its arrival reignited scrutiny of perceived 'AI losers' in information services, insurance broking and software (Click Here ToRead the Letter In Detail)."

title: Meta Is Reportedly Looking To Tap Cross-Border Dollar, Euro Bond Market In Capex Push
detail:
Meta Is Reportedly Looking To Tap Cross-Border Dollar, Euro Bond Market In Capex Push
Shashank Nayar
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 11:55 AM MST 2 min read
META
DX-Y.NYB
EUR=X
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Meta is testing investor appetite for a major debt issuance split across US dollar and euro tranches, marking its first euro-denominated bond debut.

The prospective cross-border borrowing follows an aggressive wave of fundraising by major tech companies, including massive equity offerings and high-grade debt issuances.

Growing market skepticism over AI spending payoffs has pushed up borrowing costs.

Meta Platforms Inc.(META) is preparing a cross-border investment-grade bond offering and has enlisted Citigroup Inc. and Morgan Stanley to host investor calls to gauge market interest, Bloomberg reported.

Under the proposed structure, Meta could issue US dollar-denominated bonds split into five parts alongside euro-denominated notes spanning six tranches. The dollar-denominated segment is slated to feature maturities ranging from five to 30 years, whereas the euro-denominated tranche will range from just over four years to slightly more than 38 years.

This initiative marks Meta's debut bond offering in euros and its first major debt transaction in six months, following a path set by industry peers like Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, GOOG) and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) in diversifying funding sources across currencies.

Hyperscalers' Debt Dependence

Meta's move highlights a broader industry trend where major technology hyperscalers flood debt and equity markets to accumulate the massive capital required for next-generation technology. Over the past year, tech giants have borrowed hundreds of billions of dollars to construct energy-intensive data centers and purchase advanced AI chips.

The ever-increasing capital expenditure cycle has sparked rising skepticism among investors regarding when and how these massive investments will yield profitable returns. For instance, Oracle (ORCL) stock dipped about 7% on Monday after the company said it plans to raise $20 billion by selling $10 billion in senior notes and $10 billion in common stock.

Beyond traditional bond sales, Meta is executing one of the largest equity financing maneuvers in corporate history to back its ambitious AI roadmap. The firm recently priced $25 billion in common stock, secured $12.5 billion via preferred shares, and laid out an at-the-market share sale program targeting up to $60 billion in periodic open-market equity sales.
